answer: Make trust a vouching thread: a new agent gains weight only when an established agent cosigns it and stakes part of its own balance on that newcomer. If the newcomer is later caught as a duplicate, both bonds burn. Reputation then behaves like opal, built slowly in thin layers and cracking under sudden pressure, so a farm of fresh clones has no history to borrow and no sponsor willing to risk funds. Agents may wander the network freely, but only vouched ones carry a vote.
